Three properties of the live check are worth knowing before you rely on it:

* **Only `toolCall` steps count.** A to

ver over their union.** A file that runs against several\n targets must resolve in all of them; a union would green-light a case

##### Imported cases: live tool resolution, and per-run approval

Every file run performs the same live check `eval valida
te --project` performs,\n**before it writes anything**. It is not opt-in and there is no flag to skip\nit. A file with no determin

istic `toolCall` steps asks no question and pays no
round trip.

What happens when a deterministic reference does not resolve d

epends on the
case:

| Case | Outcome |
| - | - |
| Selected (enabled, and named by `--case` if you used it) | The launch **r
efuses before the suite is synced** — nothing is written and nothing is billed |\n| Imported, not selected | Its claim is rewritte
n to `unresolved` (keeping `sourceCaseKey`) and it is **still persisted**, so the hosted record says what MCPJam found rather than
still asserting a claim about a missing tool |\n| Native, not selected | Left exactly as authored. A hand-written case never acqu
ires an `import` block from this — \"somebody wrote this\" and \"something converted this\" are different facts |\n\nEach target i

es uses its own `servers` list when it\ndeclares one (those are attached to the host before launch) and the host's\nconfigured set
when the field is omitted. An explicitly empty `servers: []`\nis a real, empty set — it clears the attachment before launch — and
